cards.text: Last time, Aaron's staff sprouted almonds overnight (Numbers 17:8). Now the LORD speaks to Aaron, Israel's priest, whose brother is Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 28:1). He starts heavy: Aaron, his sons and his father's house must bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary.

cards.question: Then God narrows it down. Who must bear the iniquity involving the priesthood?

answers.text: The leaders of all twelve tribes

cards.text: But Aaron isn't running this solo, friend. God tells him to bring his brothers from the tribe of Levi, his father's tribe.

cards.question: God says those Levites will join Aaron and ___ him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony.

cards.text: The Levites will attend to Aaron's duties and to ALL the duties of the Tent, like the new hire whose job list ends with one line: also, everything else. But there's one line they can NOT cross.

cards.question: What must the Levites not come near?

answers.text: The furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar
The poles and the outer curtains of the Tent
The courtyard gate in front of the Tent

cards.question: If the Levites cross that line, only the Levites will die.

cards.text: The Levites will join Aaron and attend to all the work at the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron attends to the duties of the sanctuary and the altar. Clear lanes, friend, like a kitchen where everybody knows whose oven is whose.

cards.question: Why does God put Aaron on the duties of the sanctuary and the altar?

answers.text: So wrath may not fall on the Israelites again
So the tribes may not quarrel over the altar again
So the Levites may not carry the load alone again

cards.text: Then God says, “Behold, I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites…” I'm leaning in, friend, because this is either a compliment or a chore chart.

cards.question: God says He selected the Levites as a ___ to Aaron, dedicated to the LORD to serve at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: But everything concerning the altar and what's inside the veil belongs to Aaron and his sons only. That's a door with one family's name on it, friend, and NOBODY else is getting a copy of the key.

cards.question: God tells Aaron that the work of the priesthood is a gift too.
What happens to any outsider who comes near the sanctuary?

answers.text: They must be put to death
They must bring a guilt offering
They must leave the camp for a week

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Aaron, “Behold, I have put you in charge of My offerings.” The sacred offerings of the Israelites go to Aaron and his sons as their portion.

cards.question: God gives Aaron and his sons this portion only for Aaron's lifetime.

cards.text: From the most holy offerings, the part reserved from the fire belongs to them: grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings. In the drawer, my portion was dust, friend, and I didn't even get the GOOD dust.

cards.question: Who may eat the most holy offerings?

cards.text: Then the offering of their gifts and all the wave offerings of the Israelites go to Aaron, his sons and his daughters, as a permanent statute. That's the whole family in on it, friend, like my six crowding the counter when the timer dinged, and Mags dinged LOUDER.

cards.question: Every ceremonially clean person in Aaron's household may eat the gifts and wave offerings.

cards.text: The list rolls on: the freshest olive oil, the finest new wine and grain the Israelites bring as firstfruits, and every devoted thing in Israel all go to Aaron. That's like opening your mailbox and finding nothing but birthday cards, friend, and not ONE bill.

The firstborn of every womb offered to the LORD, man or beast, belongs to Aaron too. But some of those firstborn have to be bought back, and friend, somebody once paid a whole quarter for me, so I RESPECT a price tag.

cards.question: Every firstborn son, and every firstborn male of ___ animals, must be redeemed.
What is the redemption price for a month-old boy?
Aaron may also redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep or a goat.

cards.text: God calls those three holy, and their blood goes on the altar and their fat is burned as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. A pleasing aroma, friend, I KNOW that one, because I've opened an oven door and had three bakers fall in love at once.

cards.question: Who does the meat of those firstborn oxen, sheep and goats belong to?
God seals all these holy offerings with a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD. Who is it for?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them.” No land, friend, and even in the junk drawer I had a little spot behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: So what does God say is Aaron's portion and inheritance among the Israelites?

cards.text: Next, God tells Aaron about the Levites, the ones doing the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they get something in return for all that work. Friend, I worked years on the Millers' counter and got paid in flour to the face.

cards.question: God gives the Levites all the ___ in Israel as an inheritance.

cards.text: No longer may the Israelites come near the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die. The Levites do the work and bear their iniquity, and they get NO inheritance among the Israelites, friend, not even a spot behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: God says the Levites get no inheritance among the Israelites because He gave them the tithe as their inheritance.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to speak to the Levites, and here's the twist: the folks who RECEIVE the tithe have to give from it too. That's like your paycheck clearing and your first move is writing a check.

cards.question: How much of the tithe do the Levites present as an offering to the LORD?

cards.text: God says their offering will be reckoned to them as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress. Grain and juice, friend, and not one cookie in sight, so I'm just going to nod politely.

cards.question: Who receives the LORD's offering from the Levites' tithes?
The Levites present the offering due the LORD from all the ___ of every gift.

cards.text: God says it again: once they've presented the best part, it's reckoned to them as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress. That line again, friend, and when God says something twice, I write it on my apron.

cards.question: The Levites and their households may eat the rest of the tithe anywhere, as payment for their work at the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: Once they've presented the best part, they won't incur guilt because of it. But God ends with a warning about the sacred offerings of the Israelites, and friend, when the last line of the recipe is a warning, you read it TWICE.

cards.question: What happens if the Levites defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites?
